quests.instruction: Identify the nature season when flowers bloom and trees grow new green leaves!
quests.question: Spring
quests.hint: Baby animals are often born during this fresh, colorful season.
quests.explanation: Yes! Spring is correct because it is the season when flowers bloom and trees grow fresh new leaves.
quests.funFact: Spring is the season right after winter, when the weather starts warming up again!

quests.instruction: Identify the nature season that is the hottest time of the whole year!
quests.question: Summer
quests.hint: Days feel longer, and the Sun stays out well into the evening during this season.
quests.explanation: Yes! Summer is correct because it is the hottest season of the entire year.
quests.funFact: Summer has the longest days of sunlight of any season of the year!

quests.instruction: Identify the nature season when leaves turn orange, red, and brown before falling!
quests.question: Autumn
quests.hint: This colorful season comes right between summer and winter.
quests.explanation: Yes! Autumn is correct because it is the season when leaves turn colorful before falling.
quests.funFact: Autumn is also called 'fall' because that's exactly when leaves fall from the trees!

quests.instruction: Identify the nature season that is the coldest time of the whole year!
quests.question: Winter
quests.hint: Many trees stand bare, and snow often covers the ground during this season.
quests.explanation: Yes! Winter is correct because it is the coldest season of the entire year.
quests.funFact: Winter has the shortest days and the longest nights of any season!

quests.instruction: Identify the nature event that brings months of heavy seasonal rain to some countries!
quests.question: Monsoon
quests.hint: Farmers in some parts of the world depend on this rainy season for their crops.
quests.explanation: Yes! A Monsoon is correct because it is the season of heavy rain that some countries depend on.
quests.funFact: Monsoon rains can bring more water in one season than falls all year in other places!

quests.instruction: Identify the nature event when no rain falls for a very long time!
quests.question: Drought
quests.hint: Rivers and lakes can shrink smaller and smaller during this long dry spell.
quests.explanation: Yes! A Drought is correct because it is a very long period without any rain.
quests.funFact: Some droughts have lasted for many years in a row in very dry regions!

quests.instruction: Identify the nature event when farmers gather ripe crops from their fields!
quests.question: Harvest
quests.hint: This is the reward for months of planting and growing crops all year.
quests.explanation: Yes! A Harvest is correct because it is when farmers gather their ripe crops from the fields.
quests.funFact: Many countries celebrate a special festival to give thanks for a good harvest!

quests.instruction: Identify the nature event when the weather stays extremely hot for several days in a row!
quests.question: Heatwave
quests.hint: People try to stay in the shade and drink extra water during this hot stretch of weather.
quests.explanation: Yes! A Heatwave is correct because it is when extremely hot weather lasts for several days in a row.
quests.funFact: During a heatwave, sidewalks and roads can even get too hot to safely touch!

quests.instruction: Identify the nature object that is a tree that stays green all year, even in winter!
quests.question: Evergreen
quests.hint: Unlike most trees, this one never loses all of its leaves or needles.
quests.explanation: Yes! An Evergreen is correct because it is a tree that stays green all year, even in winter.
quests.funFact: Pine trees are a common kind of evergreen that stay green through every season!

quests.instruction: Identify the nature object that is all the colorful leaves covering the trees in autumn!
quests.question: Foliage
quests.hint: People often travel just to see this turn bright orange, red, and yellow.
quests.explanation: Yes! Foliage is correct because it is all the colorful leaves that cover trees in autumn.
quests.funFact: Some places become famous tourist spots just because their autumn foliage is so colorful!

quests.instruction: Identify the nature season that comes right after winter ends!
quests.question: Spring
quests.hint: The weather slowly turns warmer, and gardens burst into color during this season.
quests.explanation: That's right! Spring is correct because it is the season that comes right after winter ends.
quests.funFact: Many trees that lost their leaves in autumn grow brand new ones during this season!

quests.instruction: Identify the nature season when school lets out and the weather turns warm!
quests.question: Summer
quests.hint: Families often go swimming or visit the beach during this sunny season.
quests.explanation: Great choice! Summer is correct because it is the warm, sunny season when many families go swimming.
quests.funFact: In some parts of the world, summer can last for many months without a single drop of rain!

quests.instruction: Identify the nature season when farmers gather their crops from the fields!
quests.question: Autumn
quests.hint: The air turns cooler and crisper as this season begins.
quests.explanation: That's right! Autumn is correct because it is the season when farmers harvest their crops.
quests.funFact: Squirrels are extra busy gathering nuts and seeds to store during this season!

quests.instruction: Identify the nature season when many animals grow thicker fur to stay warm!
quests.question: Winter
quests.hint: Ponds and lakes can freeze solid during this icy, cold season.
quests.explanation: Great choice! Winter is correct because it is the cold season when animals grow thicker fur to stay warm.
quests.funFact: Some places get so cold in winter that breath turns visible in the air!

quests.instruction: Identify the nature event where strong seasonal winds bring huge amounts of rain!
quests.question: Monsoon
quests.hint: This rainy season happens at roughly the same time every single year.
quests.explanation: That's right! A Monsoon is correct because seasonal winds bring it huge amounts of rain each year.
quests.funFact: Some cities plan their entire year around when the monsoon rains will begin!

quests.instruction: Identify the nature event that leaves the ground dry, cracked, and thirsty for water!
quests.question: Drought
quests.hint: Farmers worry about their crops during this long stretch without rain.
quests.explanation: That's right! A Drought is correct because it leaves the ground dry and cracked from a lack of rain.
quests.funFact: Plants and animals have special ways of surviving a long drought without much water!

quests.instruction: Identify the nature event that happens once plants have finished growing and ripening!
quests.question: Harvest
quests.hint: Trucks and baskets are busy carrying crops away from the fields during this time.
quests.explanation: That's right! A Harvest is correct because it happens once crops have finished growing and ripening.
quests.funFact: In the past, entire villages would work together to bring in the harvest each year!

quests.instruction: Identify the nature event that makes the whole week feel much hotter than usual!
quests.question: Heatwave
quests.hint: Fans and cool drinks become extra popular during this stretch of unusually hot days.
quests.explanation: Great choice! A Heatwave is correct because it makes the weather much hotter than usual for many days.
quests.funFact: Some cities open extra cooling centers to help people stay safe during a heatwave!

quests.instruction: Identify the nature object that keeps its needles even when snow covers the ground!
quests.question: Evergreen
quests.hint: This tree is often chosen and decorated during winter holiday celebrations.
quests.explanation: That's right! An Evergreen is correct because it keeps its needles even when snow covers the ground.
quests.funFact: Some evergreen trees can live for hundreds of years without ever losing all their leaves!

quests.instruction: Identify the nature object that describes all the leaves growing on a tree or plant!
quests.question: Foliage
quests.hint: A thick, healthy tree usually has plenty of this leafy covering.
quests.explanation: That's right! Foliage is correct because it describes all the leaves growing on a tree or plant.
quests.funFact: Foliage isn't just green — in autumn, it can turn brilliant shades of red and gold!

quests.instruction: Identify the nature season full of blossoms, baby birds, and warmer, sunnier days!
quests.question: Spring
quests.hint: This is often people's favorite season for planting a brand new garden.
quests.explanation: Great job! Spring is correct because it is full of blossoms and warmer, sunnier days.
quests.funFact: Rain showers are common in spring, which is why so many flowers bloom during it!

quests.instruction: Identify the nature season with the shortest nights and the most hours of daylight!
quests.question: Summer
quests.hint: The Sun rises early and sets late during this bright, warm season.
quests.explanation: That's right! Summer is correct because it has the shortest nights and the most daylight hours.
quests.funFact: Some places near the North Pole get sunlight almost all day and night during summer!

quests.instruction: Identify the nature season that comes right before the cold of winter!
quests.question: Autumn
quests.hint: Trees prepare for colder weather by dropping their leaves during this season.
quests.explanation: Great job! Autumn is correct because it comes right before winter and is when trees drop their leaves.
quests.funFact: Leaves change color in autumn because trees stop making their green coloring for the winter!

quests.instruction: Identify the nature season with the least amount of daylight all year!
quests.question: Winter
quests.hint: The Sun rises late and sets early during this dark, chilly season.
quests.explanation: That's right! Winter is correct because it has the least daylight of any season all year.
quests.funFact: In the coldest parts of winter, some lakes freeze thick enough to walk across!

quests.instruction: Identify the nature event that can flood rivers with weeks of nonstop rain!
quests.question: Monsoon
quests.hint: This rainy season is very important for filling rivers and watering crops.
quests.explanation: Great job! A Monsoon is correct because its weeks of rain can fill rivers and water crops.
quests.funFact: Without monsoon rains, some regions would not get enough water for the entire year!

quests.instruction: Identify the nature event where rivers shrink and plants struggle without enough water!
quests.question: Drought
quests.hint: This dry spell can last for many months, or even longer.
quests.explanation: Great choice! A Drought is correct because rivers shrink and plants struggle during this long dry spell.
quests.funFact: Some desert plants can survive years of drought by storing water inside themselves!

quests.instruction: Identify the nature event that fills barns and baskets with fresh crops from the field!
quests.question: Harvest
quests.hint: Farmers wait patiently all year for this important, busy time.
quests.explanation: Great job! A Harvest is correct because it fills barns and baskets with fresh crops from the field.
quests.funFact: A harvest moon is a bright, full moon that once helped farmers work late into the night!

quests.instruction: Identify the nature event where the temperature stays high day after day without cooling down!
quests.question: Heatwave
quests.hint: Even the nights stay warm during this long, hot stretch of weather.
quests.explanation: That's right! A Heatwave is correct because the temperature stays high for many days without cooling down.
quests.funFact: Heatwaves can sometimes make it too hot for some plants and animals to be active outside!

quests.instruction: Identify the nature object that never turns bare, unlike the trees around it in autumn!
quests.question: Evergreen
quests.hint: While nearby trees drop their leaves, this one stays green through every season.
quests.explanation: Great job! An Evergreen is correct because it never turns bare, staying green through every season.
quests.funFact: Evergreen needles are thin and waxy, which helps them survive through the cold winter!

quests.instruction: Identify the nature object that changes from green to fiery colors as the weather cools!
quests.question: Foliage
quests.hint: This leafy covering puts on a colorful show every single autumn.
quests.explanation: Great choice! Foliage is correct because it changes to fiery colors as the weather cools in autumn.
quests.funFact: Cooler nights and sunny days make the most brilliant, colorful foliage of the whole year!
